text:
Maria Gonzalez: Heads-up — Android sample app hitting what looks like an infinite retry loop after token refresh. Repro on Pixel 6 (API 31) when switching networks (wifi->cell), stack shows java.io.EOFException during TLS read then our auth logic replays the request repeatedly.
Jon Park: Oof. Which OkHttp / Retrofit versions?
Maria Gonzalez: OkHttp 4.11.0, Retrofit 2.9.0, Kotlin coroutines adapter. Happens with both suspend functions and enqueue. Minimal repro in the sample app.
Samir Patel: Can you paste the auth/interceptor code? Interceptor vs Authenticator ordering is a common footgun.
Maria Gonzalez: Sure — simplified snippet:
```kotlin
class AuthInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val token = tokenProvider.get()
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
      .build()
    val resp = chain.proceed(req)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      tokenProvider.refresh() // blocking refresh + update
      return chain.proceed(req.newBuilder()
         .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenProvider.get()}")
         .build())
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```
Jon Park: That explains it — doing refresh inside an Interceptor and re-calling chain.proceed can replay on the same call and confuse connection reuse. Use an Authenticator for 401 flows instead.
Maria Gonzalez: We tried Authenticator but still saw EOFException on some runs. I think keep-alive + pooled sockets + server close during network handover leads to TLS EOF, then our code sometimes treats it as a recoverable path and replays incorrectly.
Samir Patel: Right — if a socket is closed mid-handshake you'll get EOF/SSL exceptions. A few practical fixes: move refresh to an Authenticator (implements authenticate(route, response) -> new Request), make refresh singleflight/synchronized to avoid parallel refreshes, and when token changes evict the connection pool to avoid reusing sockets tied to old auth state: `okHttpClient.connectionPool.evictAll()` after refresh. Also consider `call.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for endpoints that must not duplicate.
Maria Gonzalez: Good call. Also saw a crash on rotation in the sample: NetworkOnMainThreadException — because one sample activity used `api.execute()` inside onResume for quickness.
Jon Park: For rotation / lifecycle, prefer `lifecycleScope.launch { api.listModels() }` with Retrofit suspend functions. Avoid execute() on main thread.
Maria Gonzalez: I opened a small PR with fixes + updated sample app and comments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/android-sdk-samples/pull/27. Changes: switch to TokenAuthenticator, synchronized refresh, connectionPool.evictAll() on token change, lifecycleScope usage, and tests that try to simulate network switch.
ci-bot: build passed for PR #27 — instrumented tests on API 31 are green.
Samir Patel: LGTM. Two extra suggestions: reduce idle keep-alive for mobile clients (`connectionPool = ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`) or tune it to server behavior, and add an EventListener to log connection reuse so we can debug in the field.
Maria Gonzalez: :thumbsup: will add keep-alive tuning and an EventListener. Also planning a short README note about Android pitfalls (AuthInterceptor vs Authenticator, evicting pool after refresh, lifecycle coroutines).
Jon Park: Can we add a tiny e2e test that simulates token expiry + reconnect (even if flaky) so we catch regressions?
Maria Gonzalez: Yep — adding tomorrow. Marking this thread resolved for now.
